item.title: Live: France suspends stun grenade use in school protests after 15-year-old loses hand
item.description:
France braced for more intense student-led protests, as political upheaval ripples through Europe’s major economies. French youths have been demonstrating over poor conditions at school buildings, and analysts expect unrest to intensify after a teenager’s hand was blown off by a riot police sting grenade . The country is already bitterly divided, with far-left and far-right parties leading opinion polls ahead of presidential elections next year. Germany and Spain face their own political turmoil: The former is in deadlock over tax proposals that, alongside a string of election embarrassments, threaten the governing coalition and could lead to the chancellor being ousted; the latter will hold snap elections after a key housing law failed in parliament. — Prashant Rao

item.title: Yemen's Houthis claim strikes on Aden, Riyadh airports
item.description:
Saudi-backed Yemeni forces said Monday they had expelled the Houthis from key areas surrounding the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on the Red Sea following a major counteroffensive. Reclaiming coastal areas seized during the Houthis’ lightning advance last month curtails the rebels’ ability to significantly disrupt energy flows, but the counteroffensive — a hoped-for “ zero hour ” — among some Saudi and Yemeni pundits, could widen the Iran war, further upending energy markets: Saudi Aramco’s chief told the Financial Times that global oil stockpiles are now “ scarily thin .” The kingdom’s previous war against the Houthis resulted in a yearslong quagmire and devastating humanitarian crisis, but former Saudi intelligence chief Prince Turki Al-Faisal told that restraint “ is no longer operable .” — Brendan Ruberry

item.title: Man living in Congo who went back to Kenya is country's 1st confirmed Ebola case and death
item.description:
Health minister says 28 contacts identified after death of citizen who arrived from DRC on Saturday Kenya has reported its first-ever Ebola death, the health minister announced on Tuesday, as the disease continues to spread rapidly through the north-east of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where the outbreak was announced in May. This is the 17th outbreak of the highly infectious, often deadly disease in the DRC. As of 2 October, 4,082 people had died out of 8,463 confirmed cases in the country since the emergence of the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus, for which there is still no vaccine nor specific treatment. item.title: Where is Spain headed after the snap election announcement?
item.description:
A thriving economy, a model green transition, social advances – Spain’s PM shouldn’t be in trouble. Yet he is, and it’s a lesson for progressives everywhere To progressives across the west, Spain has been a rare glimmer of hope in a world where far-right parties are increasingly entering government. Under Pedro Sánchez, who became prime minister in 2018, the country has combined a post-Covid economic boom with a bold green energy transition programme, and a pro-immigration stance with a principled opposition to the war agenda of Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu. Yet, at the end of next month, this rare beacon of democratic progress could fall. On Monday Sánchez called a snap general election , set for 29 November, after two decrees to address the country’s housing crisis were voted down in the lower chamber by politicians from rightwing parties.
